name: Peppermint
lede: Peppermint is a fresh mid green, named for the herb and the candy flavor more than for any pigment.

sections.title: A name taken from the herb
sections.body:
Peppermint is a green named from the mint plant and its sweets [3]. It is listed in the Maerz and Paul dictionary of color of 1930 [3].

The one book passage we hold mentions peppermints only as candy. St Clair tells how a Bradford sweet-maker in 1858 mixed up white arsenic and powdered sugar, and the peppermints that resulted poisoned many people [1]. It is a story about sweets and not about the color, and it says nothing about how the green got its name [1]. We stop there rather than pad [3].

The swatch on this page is #43AA5A, the screen value we hold for it, which is an approximation and not a measured pigment [3]. Like any pale color it sits between its hue and [[white]], and because the name is a description and not a tradition, other lists may place it a little differently [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Peppermint is very rare in our archive: 1 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed [2]. It is rarer than 86 percent of the named colors [2].
